It Used to Be Accessible. I’ve used this app for a long time and absolutely loved it. Every morning I’d listen to the devotionals with my kids because, as a busy mom, I don’t always have time to sit down and read everything. The audio teaching was what made this app so special.

Now I can’t even listen to the daily devotional without paying. It feels like almost everything meaningful has been locked behind a paywall. Charging $70 a year or $10 a month for a devotional app feels excessive, especially when the content used to be freely available.

And the cherry on top? A waitlist of 29,000+ people hoping someone else will pay for their subscription. That should probably tell you something.

It’s disappointing because this app used to feel like it was about making God’s Word accessible to everyone. Now it feels more like it’s about maximizing subscriptions.

Glorify’s Business Practices. Glorify started as a wonderful app that seemed to really prioritize the message of God. The call to all believers is to go forth and make disciples, and this app was doing a phenomenal job of building an intentional, daily opportunity to engage with God and grow fellow believers in Christ. However, over the years, they’ve continually drawn back on free features and now there is not much left to do at all unless you are a paid subscriber. The nature of the app itself has now changed, and what should be free for all to experience and learn in Christ is now paywalled. 

I don’t believe that there’s anything wrong with having paid features in an app, but ALL of these features started off as free, it’s astonishing to see they’ve left little unpaid now. I’m very disheartened to say that I will now be uninstalling the app. I do not wish to support a company that has changed to view believers and their faith as business models. An app now only useful for those willing to pay.

Disappointing. I’ve been a longtime user of Glorify and really appreciated the balance they initially struck between free and premium content. While some features were always behind a paywall, there was still meaningful value in the free version especially the audio daily devotionals and guided meditation walks.

Over time, however, that balance has steadily eroded. First, the guided walks became premium-only. Now, with the most recent update, even the audio component of the devotionals arguably the heart of the app are locked behind a subscription. You can’t even listen to them anymore without paying. And having a free Bible within the app might be nice, but the features are sub-par to other more reputable apps. It was the devotional pieces that drew me in, and now have left me discouraged!

It feels like Glorify waited until they had a solid user base before restricting access and pushing harder for subscriptions. I understand the need for sustainability, but the drastic shift in what’s freely available is disappointing and leaves long-time users feeling overlooked.

reviews.text:
Family Plan, Please!!!. The reason for only giving one star is about cost and the way the developers have handled the transition from an open, full-access, free service to a heavily limited, paid service. While I completely understand the need to charge for service, and have no problem paying, the way Glorify has gone about this is pretty awful. There are 4 members in my house (mom, dad & 2 kids) who use the app daily. It has been a huge blessing in our lives. For over a year we were able to each use the app daily for free, with all of its features, namely the “Listen” and “Daily Walk.” (This was especially helpful for my disabled daughter.) These were the features that set this app miles apart from others. Now, in order to be able to access the best and most used features, we have to pay $70 per year, per person. That’s $280 per year. Absolutely ridiculous and impossible for a family on a fixed income with only 1 working spouse! Again, I have no problem paying for the service, especially for one that is as valuable to our lives as this one, but come on! That’s just way too expensive, especially when it was literally just free. 
The developers do seem to be trying to help with this by offering a wait list (which is currently in the thousands), where they give one free subscription for every paid subscription. However, this does very little for families like mine. 
Please offer a family plan. At the very least, provide an option where we can pay for a subscription and choose to then gift the free one to someone specific, if we so choose. 
Until something changes, we will sadly be forced to look elsewhere.
